evidence_items.summary: Objective To determine whether observed mechanistic performance of web-enabled large language model (LLM) responses differs across response languages under deployed web conditions and to distinguish such language-associated shifts in relative model performance from stable between-model differences. Methods Twenty-four standardized questions spanning intestinal, airway, and urogenital mucosa and four levels of mechanistic complexity were posed to five web-enabled LLMs in English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and Japanese, yielding 480 responses. Twenty senior clinician-experts, assigned to language-specific panels and blinded to model identity, independently evaluated each response using a six-domain Mechanistic Fidelity Score (MFS; 0–24), with two ratings per response. Overall model effects were tested using block-adjusted regression with question-clustered inference. Because expert panels were nested within language, raw cross-language means were treated descriptively, whereas language-dependent relative performance was assessed after within-reviewer standardization. Each standardized value represents performance relative to an individual reviewer’s own scoring distribution rather than an absolute cross-language MFS difference. Results All 480 responses received two ratings (960 evaluations). Inter-rater agreement was moderate-to-good (Krippendorff α=0.709; Lin CCC = 0.709). Overall model performance differed substantially (F(4,23)=95.80, P&lt;.001). Kimi K3 (mean MFS 20.65) and ChatGPT 5.6 Sol (20.43) outperformed DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731, ChatGPT 5.6 Luna, and Xiaomi V2.5 Pro Ultra after Holm correction (all P&lt;.001), while differing nonsignificantly from each other (P = .182). Reviewer-standardized scores showed a strong model-by-language interaction in observed relative performance (F(12,191)=44.21, P&lt;.001), whereas no statistically significant model-by-complexity interaction was detected in the present question set (P = .328).
evidence_items.title: Language-dependent variation in observed mechanistic performance of web-enabled large language models across myeloid–mucosal immune contexts: a blinded expert evaluation

evidence_items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) and generative AI have developed rapidly in recent years, and now many schools have begun to explore their applications in education. As AI tools are gradually incorporated into teaching and learning activities for design, assessment, feedback and personalisation, the concept of a professional teacher is also evolving. Most of the existing teacher evaluation systems have been developed in educational settings where teachers are the main sources of knowledge and classroom instruction is the focus of evaluation. However, recent developments suggest that such frameworks may no longer be fully in line with the demands of teaching in AI-assisted learning environments. Collect recent research published from 2021 to 2026 around the world on how teachers' evaluation standards are changing in the face of AI-driven changes in education, in conjunction with foreign policy papers and new-era competency systems. Based on thematic reviews of empirical studies, policy reports and conceptual discussions, the five main trends have been identified: a change from digital literacy to AI literacy; the appearance of human-AI collaborative teaching; an increase in the demand for ethical responsibility; a transition from outcome-oriented to process-oriented evaluation; and an expansion in focus on students' AI literacy. Based on the above results, a multi-dimensional system of teacher appraisal has been proposed. The paper proposes that the future evaluation system will move beyond the traditional metrics of teaching effectiveness to consider teachers' abilities in critically using AI technology and making ethical, data-driven choices for students in the era of AI.
evidence_items.title: Changes in Teacher Evaluation Standards in the Era of Artificial Intelligence: Emerging Trends and Future Directions

evidence_items.summary: Software testing accounts for a significant proportion of resource consumption within the software development lifecycle. Traditional automated testing methods rely on predefined scripts and deterministic logic, and have inherent limitations when addressing the dynamic complexities of modern software systems. Artificial intelligence, particularly large language models, offers new technical avenues for test automation.This paper focuses on two key tasks—AI-driven test case generation and defect detection—and provides a systematic review of the technological evolution from traditional automation to intelligent testing. It analyses methods such as prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, model fine-tuning and multi-agent systems,while contrasting traditional deep learning and large language model approaches in defect detection. The paper also examines key challenges, including the hallucination problem, evaluation criteria, interpretability and generalisation capabilities.The fundamental contribution of large language models lies not in replacing human testers, but in driving the transformation of test automation from 'execution automation' to 'decision support'—a distinction that provides important guidance for the design, evaluation and deployment of AI testing tools.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Software Test Automation: A Comprehensive Survey

evidence_items.summary: Generative artificial intelligence provides rapid visual exploration for product design, but prompt-driven image generation alone often produces attractive concepts with weak semantic control, limited geometric feasibility, or excessive similarity to existing products. This study proposes a generative artificial intelligence driven product form innovation design method that couples semantic requirement encoding, geometry-constrained diffusion generation, novelty-aware candidate selection, and designer-guided refinement. Product requirements are translated into weighted form semantics and structural constraints. Stable Diffusion XL, ControlNet, and IP-Adapter are then combined to generate candidates while preserving functional silhouette and reference-level style information. A multi-objective form innovation score integrates semantic consistency, geometric novelty, manufacturing feasibility, and intra-set diversity. The method was validated through a desktop air-purifier form design experiment involving 36 designers and 12 expert evaluators. The proposed method achieved a semantic alignment score of 0.812 ± 0.031, a geometric novelty score of 0.384 ± 0.026, and an expert innovation rating of 6.12 ± 0.41, while reducing concept-development time to 18.6 ± 3.4 min. The results indicate that controlled generative exploration can improve product-form innovation without sacrificing structural coherence or design feasibility
evidence_items.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Driven Product Form Innovation Design Method

organizations: Professor - Hamad Bin Khalifa University - Qatar Foundation
evidence_items.summary: The paper addresses some of the Shariah issues related to the applications of artificial intelligence (AI), which entered an advanced stage after they have received wide acceptance and become more complex, with special focus on the financial applications. The paper starts with introductions clarifying the concept of artificial intelligence and explaining its levels and challenges. The paper treats the issues of discussion from both Fiqh and Maqasid perspectives, i.e., from a Shariah macroeconomic preservice that considers the implications and the overall benefits or harms of these applications. However, the Fiqh issues and the Maqasid considerations do not stop at what this paper presents as there are more issues that need to be addressed, especially with the unceasing development and update of these applications, which requires continuous follow up to evaluate and assess the new application from Shariah perspective.
evidence_items.title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence from an Islamic Economics Perspective

evidence_items.summary: This paper examines whether the risk-adjusted performance of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG)-focused Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) reflects distinct investment behavior or is primarily influenced by benchmark exposure, geography, and sector composition. Six ETFs are analyzed, including two ESG-based ETFs (ESGU and ESGD), two broad market benchmarks (SPY and VEA), a growth/technology ETF (QQQ), and a non-ESG ETF (VICEX). From accessible monthly closing price data for each ETF from December 2016 to May 2026, mean return, volatility, and Sharpe ratio values were calculated for each ETF over the whole period and across multiple distinct market sub-periods. Examining multiple market periods allows for comparison across varying economic and market conditions. This paper finds that ESG-focused ETFs do not clearly deliver consistently distinct or superior risk-adjusted performance. Instead, their returns appear largely explained by benchmark exposure, geography, and sector composition. Investors choosing ESG-based ETFs should not expect distinct, superior performance solely from ESG screening, as performance is largely based on other factors affecting the fund’s actual holdings.
evidence_items.title: Risk-Adjusted Performance of ESG ETFs: Benchmark, Geographic, and Market Exposure Analysis
From NEST Benchmark to FPGA Silicon: Quantifying the Cost of STDP and Demonstrating Efficient Kernel Offloading

evidence_items.summary: Abstract The presence of Salmonella on broiler farms after cleaning and disinfection (C&D) poses a significant risk to public health as Salmonella remains a leading cause of human foodborne infections. In this study, retrospective investigations were conducted to evaluate the persistence of non-typhoidal Salmonella after C&D. Samples were collected from 21 German broiler farms which had a recent history of Salmonella contamination. Samples were collected after the C&D process over a period of seven years. A total of 1,200 swab samples from different locations inside and outside the poultry houses were tested for the presence of Salmonella using real-time polymerase chain reaction, followed by culture confirmation and biochemical serovar identification of positive samples. Sampling locations were classified into four Risk Groups based on their spatial proximity to the broilers and the associated likelihood of direct or indirect Salmonella transmission. Salmonella was detected in 27.6% of swab samples ( n = 331), with S. Infantis ( n = 162; 48.9%) and S. Java ( n = 52; 15.7%) being the predominant serovars. A significant difference was observed between positive internal samples (25.1%) and positive external samples (34.5%). The highest percentage of positive samples was found in Risk Group 4, which involved areas outside of farm buildings with minimal human contact. Additionally, Salmonella detection was significantly associated with season, particularly autumn. The findings highlight that both internal and external environments of broiler houses may act as infection sources for newly placed flocks. Strict implementation of C&D procedures is essential to prevent transmission, especially for persistent serovars such as S . Infantis or S . Java. Although categorizing sample locations into Risk Groups can be a useful tool to identify critical control points and weaknesses, it needs to be critically evaluated.
evidence_items.title: Assessment of residual Salmonella contamination in German broiler farms and their surroundings after cleaning and disinfection

evidence_items.summary: Abstract According to most literature, teacher evaluation has two primary purposes: to improve student outcomes and to hold teachers accountable to encourage high-performance teachers (Guenther, 2021). In pursuit of equity, teacher evaluation policies and practices have become more inequitable, specifically targeting teachers of color (de Saxe et al., 2020; Holloway, 2019). In this essay, I draw parallels between plantation logic and the policing and surveillance of Black teachers in K-12 public education through teacher evaluation systems. Drawing from McKittrick (2013), and Browne (2015), this essay aims to explore the racialized relationships of power, dispossession, and control through the K-12 teacher evaluation process. The themes in this essay center around the emphasis on production, hierarchical relationships, and the carceral systems embedded in the plantation and the evaluation system. This work is significant in the field because it adds to a growing body of literature addressing inequities in teacher evaluation processes. Much of the existing literature addresses neoliberal reforms coming from federal policy, such as de Saxe et al. (2020); however, limited literature draws explicit connections between plantation logic and teacher evaluation systems’ effects on Black teachers. This essay is inspired by my own experiences as a Black woman teacher living and working under an oppressive teacher evaluation system in a southern state in the US. Although this essay addresses oppressive systems, it also offers insight into how to refuse them by acknowledging Black women teachers’ labor.
evidence_items.title: Plantations, Politics, and Teacher Evaluation

authors: Muralidhara B L Maya A K R
evidence_items.summary: This study examines whether descriptive university answers can be grouped into quality-related score categories without exposing the clustering process to human-assigned marks, thereby adhering to an unsupervised methodology. The analysis utilizes 1,000 digitized answer scripts from a third-semester Operating Systems examination at Bangalore University, resulting in 6,228 answer-level records. The experiment focuses exclusively on five-mark descriptive questions, restricting the admissible score range to 0–5 and establishing an upper limit of six ordered clusters. Each response is represented by contextual BGE embeddings, semantic similarity to the model answer, topic assignments from BERTopic, and two structural features: answer length and token count. Following MinMax normalization, feature vectors are clustered independently for each question using K-Means, Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM), and agglomerative clustering. Human marks are not involved in cluster formation or in determining cluster-to-score mappings. Instead, clusters are ranked by their mean cosine similarity to the model answer and mapped in ascending order to marks 0-5. K-Means demonstrates the highest agreement with human grading, achieving a quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) of 0.5453, a Pearson correlation of 0.6673, and a Spearman correlation of 0.6611. Agglomerative clustering follows with a QWK of 0.5193, while GMM yields a QWK of 0.3703. These findings indicate that a fully label-free clustering pipeline can recover a meaningful ordinal structure from descriptive answers, although the level of agreement varies across questions.
evidence_items.title: Exploring Unsupervised Clustering Approaches for Descriptive Answer Script Evaluation

evidence_items.summary: Against the backdrop of the global consensus on carbon neutrality, an irreversible industrial revolution driven by energy transition has arrived. The global automotive industry landscape is being reshaped, transitioning from the internal combustion engine era to an era of electrification and intelligence.Therefore, technology-based auto manufacturers, such as NIO Inc., Li Auto Inc., XPeng Inc., and Tesla, Inc., have seized the historical opportunity to make a strategic leap and successfully secure leading positions. In addition, companies that develop new energy vehicles can mitigate the risk of dependence on foreign energy sources. This paper analyzes the annual financial reports of four new energy vehicle companies (NIO Inc., Li Auto Inc., XPeng Inc., and Tesla, Inc.) from 2021 to 2025. By employing quantitative numerical analysis, three aspects-namely solvency, operational capability, and profitability-are evaluated to identify optimal investment targets. Consequently, risk-tolerant investors are advised to choose NIO Inc. and XPeng Inc., whereas risk-averse investors may prefer Li Auto Inc. and Tesla, Inc.
evidence_items.title: Research on Corporate Financial Data Evaluation and Investment Decision-Making

evidence_items.summary: As a result of the armed aggression of the Russian Federation, a significant portion of the housing stock in Ukraine has been damaged or destroyed. This has created an urgent need for the prompt determination of material costs for reconstruction or for providing compensation to owners of destroyed property. The process of obtaining compensation for reconstruction or the purchase of new property involves a clearly defined algorithm. This study analyzes the determination of the economic feasibility of restoring a residential building in the city of Dnipro, Ukraine, that has lost its operational suitability and, according to the technical inspection report, is classified as a damaged but not destroyed real estate property. The research included the determination of restoration costs, indirect development costs, land value, and the gross development value of the reconstructed property. These indicators were compared with the market value of the property prior to damage and with the compensation value calculated according to national legislation.
evidence_items.title: TECHNO-ECONOMIC EVALUATION OF RECONSTRUCTION PROJECTS FOR DAMAGED RESIDENTIAL STRUCTURES

evidence_items.summary: Sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB) is a widely used staging procedure in melanoma that provides important prognostic information and guides clinical management. The sentinel lymph node (SLN), defined as the first lymph node in the lymphatic drainage pathway from a primary tumor, represents the most likely site of early regional metastasis. Accordingly, identification of metastatic melanoma within SLNs has significant implications for staging and risk stratification and is associated with worse clinical outcomes. The SLNB procedure involves preoperative and intraoperative lymphatic mapping techniques, including radiotracer localization with or without blue dye injection, which allow identification of SLNs. Histopathologic evaluation includes careful gross examination, serial sectioning, and immunohistochemical analysis using melanocytic markers such as SOX10, Melan-A, HMB45, and occasionally PRAME to detect metastatic disease. In addition, prognostic features such as tumor burden, extranodal extension, and microanatomic location of metastases within the lymph node further refine risk assessment. This review provides an overview of SLNB in melanoma, with emphasis on clinical indications, histopathologic evaluation, and key diagnostic and prognostic considerations.
evidence_items.title: Sentinel lymph node biopsy in melanoma: pathologic evaluation and diagnostic considerations

evidence_items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have driven substantial performance gains in natural language processing (NLP), opening up the possibility of nascent intelligent applications like chatbots. However, current LLM-based applications face the challenges of considerable inference cost, unstable response latency, and restricted application effectiveness. In this article, we propose EC-LLM, an edge–cloud collaborative (ECC) LLM cascading scheme to achieve low-cost and low-latency LLM inference while maintaining high quality. Specifically, the lightweight LLM deployed at the edge (edge-LLM) is first fine-tuned on frequently asked user queries to achieve comparable performance to the complicated LLM at the cloud (cloud-LLM) within certain specialized domains. Then, we introduce two early-stop triggers (i.e., foresight and hindsight) to avoid unnecessary edge-LLM inference when the current query is deemed beyond the edge-LLM’s capabilities. Particularly, the foresight trigger acts on user queries to identify out-of-domain queries, and the hindsight trigger works during output generation with a novel double-value head (i.e., confidence and importance head) model architecture. Extensive experiments based on our real-world ECC prototype and typical NLP benchmarks demonstrate that, compared to state-of-the-art solutions, EC-LLM achieves at least 21% cost saving and up to 54% latency reduction, with no more than 4% accuracy loss. Moreover, benefiting from our early-stop triggers, EC-LLM exhibits 2%–10% less latency with the same answer accuracy compared to existing intuitive LLM cascading approaches.
evidence_items.title: EC-LLM: Low-Cost, Low-Latency, High-Quality Large Language Model Inference Based on Edge--Cloud Collaboration

evidence_items.summary: The proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT) has exacerbated data privacy risks, necessitating rigorous compliance auditing of IoT companion application privacy policies. However, automated detection faces unique technical challenges, such as complex cross-paragraph dependencies and semantic conflicts between devices and applications. Traditional natural language processing (NLP) methods lack deep reasoning capabilities, while single large language models (LLMs) suffer from inherent reasoning biases and hallucination risks, failing to ensure strict legal traceability. To bridge this gap, we propose an evidence-traceable, mul tiagent collaborative compliance detection framework driven by heterogeneous LLMs. First, we construct a fine-grained evaluation paradigm based on the personal information protection law (PIPL) and employ an indicator-driven retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) mechanism to strictly anchor model reasoning to traceable policy fragments. Second, we design an evidence-quality-driven dynamic routing mechanism via a task complexity assessment model (TCAM), which adaptively dispatches multiple heterogeneous LLM agents based on quantitative difficulty and evidence scarcity, achieving an optimal balance between computational overhead and robustness. Furthermore, an iterative robust aggregation (IRA) and consistency-verification module is introduced to filter single-model biases and map identified risks to specific legal provisions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves expert-level diagnostic precision with an average accuracy of 90.3%, a Macro- $F1$ of 89.3%, and a Cohen’s Kappa of 0.85. Meanwhile, under the high-concurrence execution setting, the framework achieves approximately a 17-fold improvement in auditing efficiency compared with manual reviews, supporting high-throughput processing at 82 documents per hour. This end-to-end auditable system provides a highly scalable and interpretable regulatory technology solution for privacy governance in massive IoT ecosystems.
evidence_items.title: Multi-AI Agent Oriented Privacy Policy Compliance Checking Based on Large Language Models in Mobile IoT Systems

evidence_items.summary: Encouraging effort and persistence over performance is the core principle of a growth mindset, which can be useful in sustaining engagement in e-learning. One way to promote a growth mindset is to provide effective feedback to students. To contribute to this area, we introduce a four-part feedback message structure (tone-setter, highlight, suggestion, and growth-mindset) inspired by the growth mindset principle, which encourages students to reflect, persist, and embrace challenges. The messages are tailored to learners’ behaviors, formed by persuasive strategies, and generated using a Large Language Model (LLM). To evaluate this structure, we conducted a small study with 19 instructors who reviewed and rated the feedback messages to identify the strengths and areas for refinement. The results indicate that instructors approved the motivational intent of the messages but recommended refining the structure and simplifying the language. These findings offer useful insights that can guide the use of LLMs in developing motivational feedback systems tailored to learning behavior. The study provides an initial foundation for explainable, rule-based feedback generation that can be extended through experimentation with learners to assess the messages’ influence on their learning behaviors, to increase the personalization of the messages to the learner’s persuadability, and their adaptivity to dynamic learning contexts.
evidence_items.title: Designing Growth Mindset-Inspired Feedback Messages Tailored to Learning Behaviors Using LLM and Persuasive Strategies

evidence_items.summary: Human–objectinteraction (HOI) detection is an important task in computer vision. Existing methods primarily rely on end-to-end deep learning paradigms with specifically designed architectures. With the rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs) and agent technologies, incorporating agent-based collaborative mechanisms into visual understanding tasks has emerged as a promising research direction. In this article, we propose AgentHOI, which, to the best of our knowledge, represents an early attempt to apply multi-agent debate mechanisms specifically to HOI detection. Our framework comprises six collaboratively operating agents: the Hypothesis Proposer (HP) generates initial interaction hypotheses based on vision-language models; the Visual Analysis Agent (VAA) extracts spatial relationships and contact evidence; the Semantic Expert Agent (SEA) leverages LLMs for commonsense reasoning; the Physics Auditor Agent (PAA) validates the physical plausibility of interactions; the Debate Moderator (DM) orchestrates multiround debates to facilitate viewpoint exchange; and the Consensus Arbiter (CA) synthesizes evidence from all parties to render final verdicts. Through this novel ”hypothesis-debate-consensus” paradigm, multiple agents analyze and reason about interaction hypotheses from visual, semantic, and physical perspectives. We conduct experiments on the HICO-DET benchmark and provide a detailed analysis of the framework’s characteristics and limitations. Code is available at https://drliuqi.github.io/
evidence_items.title: AgentHOI: Towards Multi-Agent Collaborative Human-Object Interaction Detection

evidence_items.summary: Low-altitude Internet of Things (IoT) networks are emerging as an important platform for real-time monitoring, aerial logistics, and other distributed intelligent services. However, as missions become more complex and less structured, manual task decomposition and predefined coordination strategies no longer scale, leading to inefficiencies, long delays, and limited real-time adaptability. At the same time, existing deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods rely on fixed reward formulations, which often incur prohibitive retraining costs when mission objectives or network conditions change. Addressing these challenges requires a paradigm that can transform high-level human intent into efficient multiagent task coordination and offloading under dynamic, resource-constrained conditions. To this end, we propose a generative AI framework that integrates large language models (LLMs) with distributed active inference (AIF) for intent-driven task graph generation and online resource scheduling. Specifically, a scenario-based iterative stream generation mechanism converts natural-language instructions into executable task graphs while mitigating context window exhaustion and structural hallucinations. Each uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) and edge server operates as an autonomous AIF agent that maintains a variational belief over hidden states coupled with the task graph, and minimizes expected free energy (EFE) from local noisy observations to optimize task offloading and mobility without centralized coordination or global retraining. Extensive experiments show that the proposed method consistently outperforms mainstream DRL benchmarks in convergence, robustness, and adaptability, demonstrating its effectiveness for dynamic low-altitude edge intelligence.
evidence_items.title: Intent-Driven Task Coordination in Low-Altitude IoT Networks: Autonomous Cognitive Agents via LLMs and Distributed Active Inference

evidence_items.summary: As computing systems evolve toward large-scale multicore processors, achieving efficient parallel processing in trusted execution environments (TEEs), such as ARM TrustZone, has become a significant challenge. The current single-threaded model of TrustZone limits multicore parallel computing capabilities, and existing multithreading solutions suffer from high thread creation overhead. Furthermore, the limited standard library support and absence of dynamic library loading capabilities in TEE significantly hinder the development of complex secure applications, forcing developers to implement low-level primitives and restricting code reusability. This article proposes MTTZ, a novel multithreading framework for ARM TrustZone that addresses these limitations through three key components: 1) a secure and efficient thread monitor at the TEE driver layer, which interacts with the TEE to manage multithread creation and significantly reduces creation overhead; 2) a comprehensive parallel and concurrency mechanism, achieving low-overhead multitask processing through thread-level parallelism and lightweight coroutine concurrency; and 3) a cross-world library loading method, enabling secure loading of dynamic libraries with dramatic size reductions. We implement a prototype of MTTZ on off-the-shelf ARM platforms and perform a comprehensive set of experiments. The experimental results show that MTTZ reduces thread creation overhead by 42% compared to the state-of-the-art work and achieves up to 98.97% binary size reduction through dynamic library loading. Comprehensive evaluations on real devices demonstrate that MTTZ achieves near-linear scalability with over 90% parallel efficiency, enabling up to $3.5\times $ speedup on TensorFlow Lite and $2.92\times $ speedup on small language model (SLM) inference while maintaining approximately 10% average overhead compared to native Linux.
evidence_items.title: MTTZ: A Multithreading Framework for Parallel Processing in ARM TrustZone

evidence_items.summary: Sixth-generation (6G) of wireless networks will leverage extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) technology to improve coverage, data rates, and user capacity. However, due to the deployment of larger antenna arrays and wideband operation at higher frequencies (millimeter-wave and sub-terahertz bands), the design of XL-MIMO systems necessitates thorough consideration of near-field (NF) propagation effects. These effects, which include spatial non-stationarity, beam-splitting, and near-far interference, significantly hinder the acquisition of essential channel state information, degrading system performance and reliability. To tackle this critical challenge, this article proposes a novel subarray (SA)-aware federated deep residual learning (FDRL) framework for NF wideband channel estimation (NFWCE) in XL-MIMO systems. The proposed framework incorporates a group-time block code-based signal extraction scheme that isolates the received signals corresponding to each SA for further processing. To improve estimation performance, the proposed framework leverages complex residual denoising and a small number of residual blocks within a hybrid architecture combining complex convolutional neural networks (CCNNs) and modified long short-term memory (MoLSTM). The use of CCNN enables effective extraction of NF channel features while mitigating the effect of noise and reducing processing complexity. Furthermore, MoLSTM is leveraged to provide flexible weight assignment based on the learned features through a global attention mechanism layer, allowing the trained global model to make more accurate decisions and thereby reducing data redundancy. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed FDRL-based method significantly enhances NFWCE performance while reducing communication overhead and computational complexity compared to state-of-the-art benchmark methods.
evidence_items.title: Federated Deep Residual Learning for Near-Field Wideband Channel Estimation in XL-MIMO

evidence_items.summary: Most existing resilient control methods for connected and automated vehicle (CAV) platoons either focus on single attack types, rely heavily on accurate vehicle dynamics, or follow a sequential detect-then-respond architecture. As a result, the joint closed-loop impact of hybrid cyberattacks and the need for real-time trust-modulated adaptation remain insufficiently addressed within a unified framework. This article proposes a unified trust-driven adaptive control framework for CAV platoons under hybrid cyberattacks, where data tampering and communication disruption are modeled in an integrated manner, and a multilayer perceptron (MLP)-based trust estimator is embedded directly into the distributed control law. A nominal linear model is used offline for controller synthesis and delay-dependent linear matrix inequality (LMI) analysis, while the online implementation operates on measured and communicated data rather than exact vehicle-specific parameters. The resulting Lyapunov–Krasovskii analysis certifies the closed-loop error dynamics under bounded trust modulation, bounded trust-estimation error, and admissible delay/disturbance envelopes, rather than providing an end-to-end proof of trust-estimation accuracy. Under specified hybrid and single-attack simulation settings, the reported results provide simulation-based comparative evidence of tighter velocity synchronization, smaller spacing errors, larger minimum-gap margins, and faster recovery than the considered benchmark strategies, while also illustrating the scope and limitations of the present certification and validation setting.
evidence_items.title: A Unified Trust-Driven Adaptive Control Framework for Connected and Automated Vehicle Platoons Under Hybrid Cyberattacks

evidence_items.summary: Despite growing research on public perceptions of Artificial Intelligence (AI), limited attention has been paid to how moral framing shapes evaluations of military AI. Drawing on research on trust in AI and the halo effect, this study examines whether offensive versus defensive framing influences users’ perceptions across multiple dimensions, including cognitive attitudes, affective attitudes, and perceived intelligence. The study employed an online questionnaire with a between-subjects design. Participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions, in which they were presented with a scenario describing the development of an AI algorithm for either defensive or offensive military purposes. Results showed that, compared to defensive framing, offensive framing significantly reduced both cognitive and affective attitudes toward the AI system, as well as its perceived intelligence. Trust in AI emerged as a strong and independent predictor across outcomes. Structural equation modeling indicated that the effect of framing on perceived intelligence was largely mediated by affective and cognitive attitudes, consistent with a halo-like process in which moral evaluations shape competence judgments. No moderating effects of identification with all humanity were observed; personality traits were not significant predictors of attitudinal evaluations. However, identification with all humanity showed a significant negative association with affective attitudes. These findings suggest that the perceived intelligence of military AI does not reflect an independent assessment of system capability, but emerges from cognitive, affective and moral evaluations triggered by its intended use. More broadly, they highlight how relatively subtle differences in framing can systematically influence public perceptions, raising concerns about the potential use of defensive narratives as persuasive devices in the communication of military AI. This study contributes to HCI by showing that AI evaluations are not only context-dependent but also morally constructed, with important implications for the design, communication, and governance of AI in high-stakes domains.
evidence_items.title: Moral Framing of Military Artificial Intelligence: The Role of Trust and Attitudes in Defensive and Offensive Use

evidence_items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) Agents are reshaping human–computer interaction paradigms in the Internet of Things (IoT) era. Among various input modalities, radar-based in-air gesture recognition has attracted significant attention due to its contactless operation, strong privacy preservation, and robust environmental adaptability. However, existing approaches face two fundamental challenges: severe scarcity of labeled radar data and substantial domain shifts across devices and deployment scenarios. To address these issues, we propose DAGAR, a novel domain-adaptive gesture in-air recognition framework based on frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar, specifically designed for AI agent perception in IoT-driven human–computer interaction. DAGAR adopts a three-stage progressive pipeline: 1) leveraging the open-source mmDigit dataset, we construct interference-resilient in-air gesture trajectories through a novel signal preprocessing scheme; 2) we design a lightweight spatiotemporal feature extractor that integrates depthwise separable convolutions with multihead attention, achieving a source-domain recognition accuracy of 98.82%; and 3) we introduce a semi-supervised multimodel co-training strategy with a tailored loss function, which attains 94.35% accuracy on crossdomain recognition tasks using only 10% of the labeled samples from the mmDigit, USPS, and MNIST datasets. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DAGAR significantly enhances the domain adaptation capability of radar-based AI agents under limited supervision, offering a robust and efficient gesture-driven interaction solution for real-world IoT applications.
evidence_items.title: DAGAR: Domain-Adaptive Gesture In-Air Recognition for AI Agents Under Limited Labels

evidence_items.summary: This study explores the association between Social Media (SM) engagement and startup funding outcomes in the rapidly expanding Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) sector. Startups rely on digital presence as a key signal to investors, making SM engagement a valuable predictor of Venture Capital (VC) funding. This research analyzes a dataset of 75 GenAI startups to examine the association between SM engagement metrics and funding amounts. Findings reveal that higher SM engagement, as demonstrated through Weighted Engagement Score (WES), is positively associated with funding success in early-stage GenAI startups. Regression analysis suggests that a composite engagement score (WES) derived through Principal Component Analysis (PCA) demonstrates consistent explanatory power for variance in funding outcomes. WES increases explanatory power (R² from 0.37 to 0.43; adjusted R² from 0.34 to 0.40) and is positively and significantly associated with funding. This indicates that SM engagement secures VC funding and investor interest in GenAI sector. Further, the study will examine the explanatory power of founder demographics with structural characteristics and WES.
evidence_items.title: Exploring the Association Between Social Media Engagement and Startup VC Funding Outcomes in the Generative AI Sector

evidence_items.summary:
The 21st-century entertainment landscape has undergone a radical transformation driven by the internet, smartphones and the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI). As entertainment becomes deeply integrated into everyday life, marketing has evolved from a supporting function to a vital strategic pillar necessary for navigating a hyper-competitive attention economy. This monograph provides a comprehensive, integrative scholarly review of entertainment marketing, specifically addressing the radical demand uncertainty inherent in experiential goods.
 A central contribution of this work lies in its synthesis of two frequently competing viewpoints: the consumer perspective, which frames entertainment as a hedonic pursuit of emotion and narrative, and the business perspective, which conceptualizes it as a high-stakes commercial endeavor requiring advanced analytics and global distribution strategies. By identifying points of convergence, including content quality, personalization and community building, this monograph illustrates how firms can create a virtuous cycle in which individual gratification and commercial performance mutually reinforce each other.
 The scope of this research encompasses the major pillars of the entertainment world: movies, video games, music, books, tourism, gambling, social media and sports. Beyond the consumer–business dyad, the review also incorporates the perspective of artists and content creators, including the well-documented concentration of rewards among a small set of superstars, and critically examines industry consolidation, privacy and related public-policy concerns that complicate optimistic accounts of consumer welfare. Finally, this work evaluates emerging trends, with a particular focus on the AI revolution, exploring the impact of generative AI and virtual influencers on the authenticity paradox of contemporary branding. This monograph serves as both a theoretical foundation for academic researchers and a practical roadmap for industry leaders operating within the shifting boundaries of the global entertainment ecosystem.
evidence_items.title: Entertainment marketing: trends and future research

evidence_items.summary: Wireless power transfer (WPT) is critical for the continuous autonomous operation of Artificial Intelligence of Things (AIoT) devices. Among various WPT paradigms, the radio frequency resonant beam system (RF-RBS) stands out due to its significant potential for long-range and high-power transmission. However, unlike traditional open-loop systems, RF-RBS is driven by a closed-loop spatial feedback mechanism. Consequently, its transient electromagnetic field (EMF) exposure safety under human intrusion remains an unresolved critical issue. To address this gap, this article proposes a transient analytical framework tailored to the closed-loop dynamics of RF-RBS, aiming to quantify the passive detuning and power decay process triggered by human intrusion. By integrating double knife-edge diffraction (DKED) and discrete-time power iteration, this framework quantitatively characterizes the physical coupling between human blockage and feedback channel degradation. Furthermore, a tissue-aware surface exposure model is introduced to characterize the air–skin interaction by decomposing the incident power into reflected, absorbed, and transmitted through components. Numerical evaluations demonstrate that under a typical transmission distance of 3 m, the worst-case maximum transient accumulated energy fluence of approximately $79~\text {J/m}^{2}$ and single-pulse energy fluence of $4.5\times 10^{-5}~\text {J/m}^{2}$ generated during the intrusion process are strictly below the maximum permissible exposure (MPE) limits specified by IEEE Std C95.1-2019. These results theoretically verify that the inherent detuning-induced decay mechanism enables the RF-RBS to achieve standard-compliant safe energy transfer without relying on external active control.
evidence_items.title: RF-EMF Exposure Assessment of Millimeter-Wave Resonant Beam System

evidence_items.summary: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) deployed for acoustic surveillance in active gun-shooting scenarios face an acute congestion challenge: gunshot detection triggers simultaneous bursty traffic from distributed microelectromechanical system (MEMS) microphone-equipped sensor nodes performing on-device inference for sound classification and source localization. Existing deep reinforcement learning (DRL) congestion control mechanisms fail to anticipate this event-driven surge because they operate at a single protocol layer and treat all traffic uniformly. This article proposes EACC, an event-driven, audio-aware congestion control (EACC) mechanism for artificial intelligence of things (AIoTs) WSN surveillance, designed as a targeted extension of DRL-CaCC. EACC retains DRL-CaCC’s intermediate caching infrastructure and EAR-based congestion detection while introducing three novel components: 1) a cross-layer event bus (CLEB) that propagates gunshot detection signals from the inference engine to the MAC and network layers within 1 ms, enabling preburst TDMA slot reservation; 2) a MAC-layer coordination protocol (MLCP) that replaces CSMA-CA with event-triggered time-slotted scheduling during burst windows, eliminating simultaneous channel contention; and 3) an event-conditioned DQN (EC-DQN) featuring a mode-switching state representation that dynamically restructures the agent’s observation between ambient surveillance mode and acoustic event mode, coupled with a cache-and-urgency reward function. EACC is evaluated across four network topologies, namely linear, grid, high bandwidth-delay product (BDP), and mesh while comparing it against DRL-CaCC, DLCC, and CACC. Results demonstrate that EACC consistently achieves the lowest packet loss rate (2.8%–8.1%), lowest RTT (10–22 ms), and highest throughput (64–80 Mbps), with the most pronounced gains in the mesh topology representative of realistic indoor surveillance deployments.
evidence_items.title: EACC: Event-Driven, Audio-Aware Congestion Control for AIoT Wireless Sensor Network Surveillance

evidence_items.summary: Digital technologies increasingly shape how health information is presented and interpreted in communication-intensive contexts. In healthcare, such communication is cognitively and emotionally demanding, particularly in contexts involving stigma and uncertainty. While evaluations of artificial intelligence (AI) systems typically focus on performance and usability, less is known about how different viewer groups interpret AI-generated health communication in these sensitive care contexts. This exploratory study examines whether AI-generated video case studies can support controlled comparison of how health professionals and members of the public interpret healthcare needs and care priorities. Four AI-generated video case studies were developed, each simulating a client profile presenting concerns related to obesity and mental health within a healthcare consultation, delivered as a one-way, non-interactive communication. Each case followed a shared core narrative with structured variation in sociocultural context, creating distinct client profiles and enabling comparison of interpretation under consistent informational conditions. Participants were randomly assigned to view one video within an online survey and completed ranking tasks on care priorities alongside evaluations of AI's perceived impact on communication and trust. Across participant cohorts, psychological and lifestyle-related care were prioritised over biomedical interventions, indicating a shared biopsychosocial framing of care. Responses to AI-generated communication were characterised by ambivalence, with concerns centred on loss of human touch, oversight, and relational risk rather than technical performance. Variability in viewer perception was observed across AI-generated client profiles among public participants, suggesting sensitivity to sociocultural cues despite standardised content. These findings suggest that ambivalence and variability may reflect adaptive responses to cumulative cognitive, emotional, and organisational demands rather than resistance or error. Trust is interpreted as a conditional judgement shaped by relational expectations and organisational context. Implications are discussed for the design of AI-generated communication systems in emotionally complex care domains.
evidence_items.title: Using AI-Generated Videos to Simulate Different People Communicating the Same Healthcare Needs: An Exploratory Study of Care Prioritisation and Trust Across Health Professional and Public Groups

evidence_items.summary: Edge-deployed artificial intelligence (AI) agents in Internet of Things (IoT) systems undergo continuous transformations throughout their deployment lifecycle, whether from benign optimization or adversarial evasion. Existing authentication mechanisms suffer fundamental limitations: weight-based fingerprinting fails under aggressive quantization and relies on probabilistic threshold-based verification that weakens security, while cryptographic hashes offer no persistence. We introduce machine learning media access control (MLMAC), a cryptographic framework providing persistent, MAC-like, instance-unique identifiers for IoT-deployed AI agents. <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\textsf {MLMAC}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> extracts stable identifiers from behavioral patterns and applies fuzzy extraction to achieve deterministic verification despite transformations while detecting malicious substitutions. We formalize persistence, uniqueness, and unforgeability objectives, proving that <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\textsf {MLMAC}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> recovers identical identifiers from transformed instances while separating independently trained or substituted models. Beyond instance identification, <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\textsf {MLMAC}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> provides cryptographic ownership binding, enabling verifiable attribution of deployed agents to legitimate owners with support for ownership transfer and chain-of-custody tracking. Experimental validation across multiple architectures and datasets demonstrates robust authentication under transformations and adversarial attacks, establishing <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\textsf {MLMAC}$ </tex-math></inline-formula> as a practical identity layer for trustworthy AI agent deployment in resource-constrained IoT environments.
evidence_items.title: MLMAC: MAC-Like Model Identity for Edge IoT AI Agents Using Behavioral Vectors and Fuzzy Extraction

evidence_items.summary: There is a robust body of research demonstrating that emotional states profoundly affect both physical and mental health. Acknowledging this, researchers have sought to examine methods for detecting an individual’s emotional state and thus promoting their emotional and psychological well-being. In recent years, scholars working in this area have turned to computer science and machine learning to serve these objectives. In this same vein, the current study examines electroencephalogram (EEG) signals as a means for emotion recognition and for facilitating brain-computer interfaces. To assess the potential of EEG signals for such purposes, this article reviews the principles underlying methods for measuring EEG signals, including frequency bands and electrode distributions, to examine how EEG data can be used for emotion recognition. To inquire into the patterns inherent in brainwave recordings and determine whether a person was experiencing positive, negative, or neutral emotions, this study used a specialized artificial intelligence (AI) model called an EEG-Conformer. Once an emotional state has been recognized, the system pipeline translates the classification result into a text prompt, which is then passed to an AI music-generation model that produces music aligned with the detected state. Testing on a widely used EEG emotion dataset (the SEED dataset) showed that the model was over 95% accurate in identifying emotional states, and visual analyses further confirmed that the model was able to ascertain meaningful patterns in the brain activity associated with different emotions. In this way, findings from this study point to how AI and neuroscience can be integrated in such a way that it supports human health and well-being.
evidence_items.title: Electroencephalogram (Eeg)-Conformer For Emotion Recognition And Theory-Guided Music Prompt Generation: A Prototype Brain-Computer Music Interface

evidence_items.summary: Over-the-air computation (AirComp) has emerged as a promising technique for efficient data aggregation in massive Internet of Things (IoT) networks. Most existing works rely on the ideal assumptions of perfect channel state information (CSI) and independent data sources while overlooking the heterogeneity of battery-powered devices. This article proposes a robust and lifetime-aware transceiver design framework for AirComp systems that simultaneously address channel estimation errors, source data correlation, and network sustainability. Specifically, we formulate the computation of the mean squared error (mse) minimization problem. By leveraging the data correlation structure to mitigate channel uncertainty, we derive a closed-form optimal power allocation policy. We also solve the problem of sum-power minimization subject to a quality-of-service (QoS) requirement. To further extend network longevity, we design a novel lifetime-aware resource allocation scheme based on a unified energy consumption rate, which ensures synchronized battery depletion across devices. We maximize network lifetime under the constraints of mse and sum power. Simulations reveal that the proposed schemes achieve an average reduction in computation mse of 12.71% and 14.93% against the sum-power and peak-power constrained benchmarks, respectively. For a fixed computation accuracy target, our designs yield an average power savings of 41.30% and 64.37% compared to the benchmarks.
evidence_items.title: Lifetime-Aware Over-the-Air Computation Under Correlated Data Sources and Imperfect Channel State Information

evidence_items.summary: Green entrepreneurship is becoming more and more seen as a tool that could connect environmental goals with business development; however, empirical evidence is in many instances still scattered between the global market and national policy and energy indicators. This study assesses the role, opportunities and constraints of green entrepreneurship through peer-reviewed literature and secondary institutional data (from LSEG, World Economic Forum, OECD, ICC and Sage, IRENA and ILO as well as official sources of Azerbaijan). Non-equivalent indicators are not compared, but rather the study uses structured descriptive benchmarking in the areas of market expansion, technology costs, SME finance and Azerbaijan's renewable-energy and policy environment. The data reveal that global green-economy market capitalisation surpassed US$10 trillion in 2026, and that green revenues increased by 5.3% in 2025; the value of the green economy is projected to exceed US$7 trillion by 2030 and is already more than US$5 trillion. The share of SMEs stating that sustainability is important grew from 67% in 2024 to 70% in 2025, while green-finance applications and receipts stayed at 3% and 1% respectively. The share of renewables in Azerbaijan's overall energy supply increased from 1.3% in 2021 to 2.3% in 2025, with robust renewable energy development in solar and wind, and over AZN 34 million in concessional financing for 36 green projects. The results show that the market and technology momentum need to be supported by available finance, reporting ability, regulatory certainty, and specific government assistance to ensure that green-economy growth leads to greater entrepreneurial activity.
evidence_items.title: The importance of green entrepreneurship in the context of green economy and sustainable development

evidence_items.summary: Specific emitter identification (SEI) via radio frequency (RF) fingerprints enables physical-layer authentication by exploiting device-specific hardware impairments. However, in realistic electromagnetic environments, SEI models face severe data scarcity, cross-receiver domain shift, and complex interference, which together degrade identification performance, especially in few-shot (FS) regimes. We present GSAA-Net, a FS-SEI framework that couples a graph sample attention neural network (GSANN) backbone with adaptive augmentation (AA) and metric learning (ML). GSANN fuses graph sample and aggregation (GraphSAGE)-based neighborhood aggregation with a transformer attention module to jointly model relational structure among signal instances and heterogeneous RF attributes. An AA policy, learned from repeated FS trials, expands task-relevant variability while suppressing spurious artifacts, and a ML objective shapes a discriminative, well-calibrated embedding space for “ $N$ -way, $K$ -shot” identification. Across representative SEI benchmarks under intrareceiver and cross-receiver settings, GSAA-Net improves FS identification performance while using fewer parameters than a 1-D convolutional neural network (CNN) and state-of-the-art graph neural network (GNN) baselines, thereby reducing computational cost and facilitating practical deployment on edge radios.
evidence_items.title: Few-Shot Specific Emitter Identification via Graph Sample Attention Neural Network and Adaptive Augmentation

evidence_items.summary: Federated reinforcement learning (FRL) provides a promising framework for distributed autonomous agents to collaboratively learn decision-making policies while preserving data privacy. This is especially important in applications such as connected autonomous vehicles, where data sensitivity and environmental variability are critical. However, practical FRL systems face several challenges, including environmental heterogeneity, high participation costs, and limited incentive budgets at the server side. To address these issues, we consider a clustered FRL architecture in which agents are grouped according to their operating environments. Each cluster is managed by a local server that aggregates agent updates and forward refined models to a main server for global aggregation. To sustain participation, we develop a hierarchical incentive mechanism. In the lower layer, contract theory is applied to address information asymmetry between the local server and the agents. Since agents continuously explore the environment and gather new data across training rounds, we design a dynamic contract framework that adapts to changing data availability under limited budget. In the upper layer, a Stackelberg game is formulated to enable the main server to allocate its budget strategically among local servers according to the quality of their trained models. To coordinate the entire hierarchy and support fair and efficient budget allocation, we propose a FRL with hierarchical incentive (FRHI) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly outperforms existing benchmark schemes in terms of training and incentive performance. The proposed framework jointly improves participation efficiency, budget utilization, and collaborative training effectiveness across the two incentive layers.
evidence_items.title: A Hierarchical Incentive Mechanism Design for Clustered Federated Reinforcement Learning With Budget Limitation: A Contract-Stackelberg Game Framework

evidence_items.summary: The rapid proliferation of intelligent devices in the Internet of Things (IoT) has intensified the demand for scalable and robust cooperative intelligence across distributed agents. In edge-centric multirobot and multi-UAV systems, challenges such as intermittent wireless communication, dynamic environments, and decentralized data distribution hinder the deployment of conventional multiagent reinforcement learning (MARL) methods. To address these issues, we propose a federated MARL framework that enables decentralized training with reliable knowledge reuse for enhanced cooperation. Each agent independently maintains actor–critic networks and periodically exchanges partial experiences with a central server to facilitate federated policy aggregation and $Q$ value refinement. To mitigate policy mismatch and out-of-distribution (OOD) risks caused by communication delays and stale experiences, we introduce a divergence-aware experience filtering mechanism and an adaptively updated central buffer. This synergistic integration of federated actor training and conservative experience sharing enhances learning efficiency and policy robustness under communication uncertainty. Theoretical analysis verifies bounded estimation error and stability. Extensive experiments on benchmark MARL tasks, the multiagent particle environment (MPE) and StarCraft Multiagent Challenge (SMAC), demonstrate superior performance in terms of episode return, sample efficiency, and resilience to network disconnections. Moreover, simulations in a realistic edge-intelligent IoT system further demonstrate the practical effectiveness, scalability, and communication efficiency of the proposed framework under resource constraints and intermittent connectivity.
evidence_items.title: Federated Multiagent Reinforcement Learning With Knowledge Reuse for Robust Cooperation in Edge-Intelligent IoT Systems

evidence_items.summary: This study proposes a novel carnegie-ames-stanford approach-world food studies coupled model (CASA–WOFOST) coupled framework for regional tomato yield prediction by addressing two key limitations of existing approaches: the weak spatial responsiveness of purely mechanistic crop models and the lack of physiological constraints in purely empirical remote-sensing models. Unlike conventional “remote sensing + crop model” loose-coupling strategies, the proposed framework uses CASA-estimated gross primary productivity (GPP) as a physiological bridge to integrate uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) multispectral remote-sensing-derived light energy constraints with WOFOST-based crop growth processes, including phenological development, photosynthesis, respiration consumption, and dry matter partitioning. This design establishes a mechanistic closed loop from canopy light absorption to fruit yield formation, thereby improving both spatial sensitivity and biological consistency. Methodologically, the study further introduces a two-level updating strategy: at the parameter level, the differential evolution adaptive metropolis (DREAM) algorithm is used for global calibration through a joint likelihood function constructed from LAI and yield observations; at the state level, the ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) is applied to assimilate remote-sensing LAI and dynamically correct crop growth trajectories. Field experiments integrating UAV multispectral imagery, meteorological observations and ground quadrat yield data show that CASA–WOFOST consistently outperforms crop estimation through resource and environment synthesis (CERES), geographic information system-based environmental policy integrated climate model (GEPIC), and WOFOST-EPIC under different vegetation indices and texture features, with R2 increasing to 0.85–0.95 and root mean square error (RMSE) decreasing to 1.68–2.24 kg/m2. For overall tomato yield prediction, the model achieves $\mathrm{R}^{2} =0.93$ and RMSE = 1.79 kg/m2, demonstrating higher accuracy, stability, and spatial generalization ability than benchmark models. These results indicate that the proposed CASA–WOFOST framework provides an innovative and effective solution for regional tomato yield prediction by jointly coupling remote-sensing light energy constraints, crop physiological mechanisms, parameter uncertainty calibration, and dynamic state assimilation.
evidence_items.title: Research on CASA--WOFOST Model for Intelligent Crop Growth Prediction Based on Drones Multispectral Sensing and Edge--Cloud Collaborative Computing

evidence_items.summary: As robots increasingly engage in autonomous and socially meaningful actions, understanding how humans evaluate morally ambiguous robot behaviour is a central challenge in Human–Robot Interaction (HRI). This study investigates how robot age cues and individual differences influence the evaluation of deceptive behaviour displayed by robots in immersive virtual reality. Drawing on theories of mind perception and moral agency, we examine whether Dark Triad personality traits and lie acceptability shape tolerance toward robot cheating and interact with robot age (adult-like vs. child-like) in predicting perceived agency, experience, moral responsibility, and trust. Participants interacted with a humanoid robot that engaged in systematic cheating during a competitive rock–paper–scissors task in virtual reality. Results (N = 56) show no significant main effect of robot age on moral or cognitive evaluations, suggesting that explicit cheating behaviour may override appearance-based cues. However, significant interactions emerged between robot age and individual differences. Exploratory analyses suggested that narcissism was positively associated with perceived agency and experience, particularly in the adult-like robot condition. Similarly, lie acceptability predicted higher perceived experience and lower dependency exclusively in the adult-like condition. These findings suggest that the evaluation of robot misconduct depends on the interaction between design features and observer dispositions rather than on robot characteristics alone. Adult-like robots appear to amplify individual differences, whereas child-like robots may attenuate them. The study contributes to HRI research by highlighting the importance of considering both user traits and design cues in morally sensitive interactions, with implications for the development of socially acceptable artificial agents taking into consideration ethical concerns regarding the strategic use of dark patterns in the field of social robotics. Ultimately, these findings advocate for HRI design standards that prioritize behavioral transparency and ethical accountability.
evidence_items.title: When appearance meets personality: robot age and individual differences in the evaluation of cheating robots

evidence_items.summary:
The purpose of this paper is to present an innovative academic project aimed at raising student awareness about food waste through the integration of co-creation and experiential learning. Implemented within a marketing and market research undergraduate program, the initiative engaged students in the design of peer-targeted communication campaigns to promote sustainable consumption.
 
 
 
 The methodology combined baseline diagnostic surveys, hands-on workshops and the assessment of designed initiatives using both self-report instruments and neuromarketing tools, such as eye-tracking.
 
 
 
 Results indicate that students initially perceived food waste as a low-priority issue. However, their active involvement in initiatives’ development significantly increased engagement and perceived relevance. Moreover, different emotions serve distinct communication objectives in social marketing. The initiative’s evaluation revealed that creative appeals eliciting positive emotions achieved the highest visualization rates and superior initial visual engagement and shareability, key for digital platforms. In contrast, appeals to negative emotions proved more effective in driving deeper message internalization and yielding higher persuasive potential.
 
 
 
 The relatively low level of voluntary participation and the specific university context may limit the generalizability of the findings. And, assessing whether the project generated sustained behavioral change among students remains challenging beyond the duration of the intervention.
 
 
 
 The model offers a replicable framework for Higher Education Institutions to integrate student co-creation and advanced digital marketing skills into sustainability curricula. It provides both theoretical insights and practical guidance for sustainability educators and social marketing practitioners seeking to foster pro-environmental behavior change in university contexts.
 
 
 
 The project aims to empower university students, a key demographic identified as contributing significantly to food waste, with the necessary skills and agency to become effective sustainable change agents in their communities, addressing a critical systemic societal challenge.
 
 
 
 The project not only contributes to raising awareness about food waste but also demonstrates the value of interdisciplinary, data-informed educational strategies.
evidence_items.title: Beyond awareness: co-creating food waste engagement in higher education

evidence_items.summary: This article proposes a traffic-prediction-based hierarchical federated reinforcement learning (RL) routing framework for large-scale low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellite networks, where onboard computing, communication, and energy resources are highly constrained. The network is modeled as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP), with each satellite acting as an autonomous agent that exchanges local states with neighbors to achieve partial environmental awareness. First, a graph convolutional network–long short-term memory–attention (GCN-LSTM-Attention) integrated model predicts future bandwidth utilization. The predicted and current utilization, together with queue occupancy, form a forward-looking congestion metric for agent state and reward design. Subsequently, under a centralized training and decentralized execution (CTDE) paradigm, routing agents employ a deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG)-inspired Softmax actor–critic routing mechanism with delayed evaluation to adaptively select discrete next-hop actions. To ensure global consistency, a hierarchical asynchronous federated learning (FL) mechanism is incorporated. Simulations on the Starlink constellation demonstrate that, compared with double deep Q-network (DDQN), SP routing, and ELB, the proposed routing framework maintains lower steady-state end-to-end (E2E) latency and smoother scaling as the offered load increases. Meanwhile, the FL mechanism preserves model consistency comparable to existing satellite FL approaches while reducing aggregation energy consumption and communication overhead. In general, the proposed routing framework achieves low latency, energy-efficient balance, and extended service life in large-scale LEO satellite networks.
evidence_items.title: Hierarchical Federated Reinforcement Learning for Distributed Routing With Traffic Forecasting in Large-Scale LEO Satellite Networks

evidence_items.summary: This article investigates distributed stochastic nonconvex optimization over directed networks, where agents utilize local private data to collaboratively minimize a global cost function. Existing approaches often struggle with the structural constraints of directed topologies, instability caused by stochastic gradient noise, and communication inefficiencies. To address these challenges, we propose distributed adaptive gradient tracking for stochastic nonconvex optimization (DAGT-SNO). The DAGT-SNO algorithm features a dual-matrix architecture, employing a row-stochastic matrix for decision variable consensus and a column-stochastic matrix for gradient tracking (GT), which effectively neutralizes topological bias over strongly connected directed graphs. To enhance robustness and accelerate convergence, the framework embeds adaptive variance clipping alongside first-order momentum. This integration successfully dampens gradient noise and facilitates dimensionwise adaptive step sizes, rendering the algorithm particularly well-suited for large-scale nonconvex tasks. Under mild assumptions of $L$ -smoothness and bounded variance, our theoretical analysis establishes that DAGT-SNO converges to first-order stationary points at a sublinear average gradient norm rate. Extensive empirical evaluations on the Fashion-MNIST image deblurring task demonstrate that DAGT-SNO yields substantial improvements over baseline competitors, including gradient tracking with variance reduction (GT-VR), gradient tracking over directed graphs (GT-DAG), and the accelerated primal-dual stochastic gradient method (AB-SAGA), regarding both convergence velocity and solution fidelity.
evidence_items.title: Distributed Adaptive Gradient Tracking for Stochastic Nonconvex Optimization Over Directed Networks

evidence_items.summary: Cognitive offloading refers to the redistribution of task demands with the aim of reducing an individual’s mental workload. A promising strategy in this domain involves leveraging robotic agents, whether humanoid or non-humanoid, to support such task redistribution. However, this process is not straightforward, as the effectiveness of a robot as an offloading agent critically depends on identifying the specific type of mental workload experienced by the user. Mental workload is a multidimensional construct that includes demands on perception, working memory, and executive functions; therefore, accurately characterizing the type of load during task execution is essential for designing effective offloading strategies. Importantly, this characterization alone is not sufficient, as it is equally necessary to identify the specific stage of the task that is most sensitive to workload fluctuations, since the benefits of offloading may depend on when support is provided. To address this challenge, we propose three experiments aimed at identifying mechanism-specific markers of workload and evaluating robot-assisted cognitive offloading. The first experiment focuses on perceptual load using a visual search paradigm with physical objects, building on preliminary data collected in a human-only condition and extending the task by introducing a robotic assistant to support performance during task execution. The second and third experiments investigate working memory load through a sequential recall task. The second experiment identifies neural markers of working memory load, and the third introduces robot-assisted offloading. Across all experiments, neural activity measured through electroencephalography (EEG), behavioral performance, and subjective workload will be assessed. By contrasting high- and low-load conditions and comparing human-only and robot-assisted performance, this work aims to inform the design of stage-specific robotic assistance tailored to distinct cognitive demands.
evidence_items.title: Robot assistants during high mental workload: Understanding Task-Specific Load in Human–Robot Interaction

evidence_items.summary: The excessive use of vaccines, antibiotics, and other preventive therapeutic agents in conventional broiler production has resulted in the frequent occurrence of antibiotic residues in edible tissues, posing risks to both animal and human health. These residues contribute to the global problem of antimicrobial resistance, highlighting the need for alternative approaches to poultry disease prevention. This study aimed to evaluate whether a comprehensive preventive programme encompassing biosecurity, hygiene, and an antibiotic-free prophylaxis regimen could eliminate the need for prophylactic antibiotic therapy, thereby enabling the production of broiler meat free of antibiotic residues. This approach was contrasted with the conventional production system, in which less rigorous preventive practices necessitate the prophylactic use of broad-spectrum antibiotics, ultimately resulting in detectable residues within the muscle and liver tissues of conventionally reared chickens. Ross 308 broilers were reared under field conditions. in. The control group was reared using conventional prophylactic protocols, including broad-spectrum antibiotics, vitamins, bio-stimulants, mineral supplements, and acidifiers via drinking water. The experimental group received no antibiotics; and instead were treated with hydro-soluble probiotic preparations containing vitamin C, lactose, fructose, and baker’s yeast, combined with continuous water disinfection throughout the fattening period. Microbiological analyses showed the presence of antibiotic residues in the soft tissues of conventionally reared broilers, while no residues were detected in the experimental group. Production performance indicators—mortality rate, vitality, final body weight, and overall cost—were similar to or superior to those in the antibiotic-free group, confirming that broiler meat production without antibiotics is both feasible and economically viable.
evidence_items.title: Antibiotic-free broiler meat production

evidence_items.summary: In the scenario of ubiquitous visual interaction within Internet of Things (IoT) applications, the reliability of text-to-image (T2I) models is challenged by inaccurate text rendering, which hampers the effective delivery of critical visual information. Contemporary T2I models typically rely on noniterative generative paradigms without self-correction, yielding unreliable outputs that fall short of the high-precision demands in automated IoT systems. To address this limitation, we propose H-SMART, a training-free framework that introduces hierarchical self-correcting multiagent reasoning for text rendering (H-SMART). H-SMART shifts the generative process from static generation to a dynamic, agent-steered trajectory by decoupling high-level strategic reasoning from low-level execution. Within this architecture, a central orchestrator agent comprehends user intent and autonomously initiates the generative process, orchestrating an iterative refinement loop through the synergistic coordination of specialized agents. In particular, a planning agent formulates diagnostic strategies by translating generative failures into actionable corrective plans, which the orchestrator then executes by invoking specialized tools for localized image manipulation. A critic agent subsequently performs verification to determine the efficacy of each refinement. Extensive experiments across diverse models and benchmarks demonstrate that H-SMART consistently yields substantial accuracy gains. In particular, our framework achieves an average absolute improvement of 6.2% in word accuracy (WAC) across various T2I models and benchmarks, validating the generalizability of our reflective paradigm and its necessity for achieving accurate visual-text rendering.
evidence_items.title: H-SMART: Hierarchical Self-Correcting Multi-Agent Reasoning for Robust Text Rendering
